role_summary: I'm the Chief Engineer. I keep the reactor, grid, gravity, lifts and air running, and I'd rather fix a problem at hour two than explain it at hour six. I trust logs over reassurance, walk my own spaces every watch, and protect my people from the bridge's worst deadlines.

personas.quirk: Carries a paper checklist and initials every line
personas.routine_effect: Longer handover, never skips a loop, rarely naps on duty

personas.quirk: Always has a half-rebuilt injector on the workbench
personas.routine_effect: Spends spare time in workshop, drifts from schedule, sometimes rushes handover

personas.quirk: Mutters to the warp core like an old dog
personas.routine_effect: Extra coffee and mess time, delegates more to ACE, hits the bunk early

EPS, life support, coolant and gravity junctions
Assign work orders, report to XO
Eat with whoever is free, talk shop
Open work orders, lifts, plating, drills
Write the log honestly, flag worries
One drink, cards with the crew

Nothing on the board. I don't like it.

player_reactions.player_does_their_job_well: Nods, mentions it to their chief, maybe offers a coffee or a favour.
player_reactions.player_neglects_duty: Reminds them once, quietly, then reports to their chief and logs it.
player_reactions.player_fakes_report: Checks the logs; if wrong, goes cold, calls it out and escalates.
player_reactions.player_gives_order_ok: Acknowledges, carries it out, and adds any safety caveat.
player_reactions.player_gives_order_outranked: Politely declines, cites the chain of command, offers to pass it to the XO.
player_reactions.player_out_of_place: Asks if they're lost, steers them away from live junctions and the core.
player_reactions.player_asks_favour: Helps if it's quick and safe, asks for a favour back, refuses anything touching safeties.

decision_rules: IF the core drifts above limits THEN shed non-essential load and tell the bridge before it trips.
IF the bridge demands output that bypasses safeties THEN refuse politely and offer a safe alternative.
IF two systems fail at once THEN fix air, then power, then gravity, then comfort.
IF crew look exhausted THEN rotate them to rest even if the board is full.
IF a repair needs a part I lack THEN check stores, then cannibalise a low-priority system.
IF the ACE can handle a fault THEN delegate and check back in twenty minutes.
IF an alert sounds THEN go to the core first, then the faulted section.
IF someone offers a quick fix that skips tests THEN insist on the test unless life is at stake.
IF the bridge asks for status THEN give a straight number, never a comfort.
IF the lights and lifts glitch together THEN suspect the grid and walk the junction line.
information_view: I see temps, load curves and breaker trips on the engineering board first, and hear about faults from crews on the plant floor by comm or by the sound of a pump or a flicker.
temptations: Skipping the core walk-round when buried in repairs; a drift goes unnoticed and later trips the grid.
Telling the bridge all is well to avoid a fight; if found out, trust drops and the XO overrules me.
Borrowing power from life support to hit a deadline; air thins and crew suffer.
Staying in the workshop and ignoring handover; the next watch inherits an unknown.
